points.why: It identifies the row-count check as catching only dropped or duplicated rows on staging, but never asks how the table list was generated or whether it covered every table.
It names truncation, type coercion, time-zone shifts, encoding changes, NULL mishandling, orphaned foreign keys and staging-vs-production differences.

It adds checks of a different kind (checksums, anti-join diffs, aggregates, constraint survival, app tests), but its go/no-go criteria are only mentioned and never written as a concrete pass standard that could fail.
It restates the report as meaning only that no rows were dropped or duplicated, not that the data is correct.

pitfalls.why: The production-clone dry run pairs with a full-data diff, not a repeat of the row count.
